finding.summary: exclusions_section.get("patterns", []) is passed straight to normalise_patterns without any type validation. In TOML, `patterns = "secrets"` (a string instead of a list) is valid and will be iterated character-by-character, producing bogus patterns like **/s, **/e, **/c... The user's intended exclusion (e.g. secrets/) is then silently NOT applied, so a file the user believed was excluded can be sent to the LLM — the opposite of this PR's fail-loud/exclusion guarantee.
finding.fix: Validate the value before use: `patterns = exclusions_section.get("patterns", [])`; if `not isinstance(patterns, list) or not all(isinstance(p, str) for p in patterns)`, print an ERROR naming the offending key and sys.exit(1), consistent with how a missing --config file is handled.
